boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Truman rituals, symbols, campus legends, and annual practices with strong visual anchors.

cards.title: The Bulldog Mascot
cards.subtitle: A school-spirit symbol adopted during the 1915 season
cards.notes: Spot Spike or the Bulldog imagery at a campus event, then use the official history to trace why students adopted this tenacious mascot.
cards.short_summary: Truman’s Bulldog identity began as a response to a losing streak.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says the student body adopted the bulldog in 1915 to revive spirit after several losing football seasons; baseball used the name that season and football the next year.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Observe mascot imagery at public campus events; event access may vary.

cards.title: Purple and White Since 1902
cards.subtitle: The school colors tied to Truman’s first school song
cards.notes: Wear purple or white for a campus gathering and listen for references to the song that established the University’s enduring color tradition.
cards.short_summary: A 1902 school song gave Truman its purple-and-white identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman identifies purple and white as school colors dating to Basil Brewer’s 1902 song, “The Purple and the White.”
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Participation can be as simple as wearing colors you already own.

cards.title: Purple Friday
cards.subtitle: Weekly purple-wearing across Truman’s campus
cards.notes: On a Friday, wear purple or Truman apparel and look for the student gatherings and music on the Mall described by the University.
cards.short_summary: Fridays turn campus purple through a shared show of Bulldog spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes every Friday as Purple Friday, when students, faculty, and staff wear purple; the tradition also includes Student Union gatherings and Mall music.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Wear purple on a Friday; specific gathering details vary by week.

cards.title: Homecoming’s Pep Rally and Parade
cards.subtitle: A fall tradition on campus since 1939
cards.notes: Check the official Homecoming schedule, then choose a public pep-rally or parade viewing spot to see a long-running Truman ritual in action.
cards.short_summary: A 1939 celebration grew into Truman’s annual weeklong Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman’s Homecoming history states that the first event occurred November 3, 1939 and became a school tradition each fall, with pep rally and parade among its continuing elements.
cards.access_notes: Consult the official Homecoming schedule for current event details and access.

cards.title: National Truman Spirit Day
cards.subtitle: The first Friday in October
cards.notes: Mark the first Friday in October by wearing Bulldog purple or Truman apparel, or decorate a personal space with Truman gear if appropriate.
cards.short_summary: The University sets aside one October Friday for visible Truman pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman invites everyone to observe National Spirit Day on the first Friday in October by wearing Bulldog purple or Truman apparel and decorating homes, offices, or vehicles with Truman gear.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: No campus attendance is required; use apparel or decorations you already have.

cards.title: The Big Event
cards.subtitle: A one-day, student-run Kirksville service project
cards.notes: Register through the SERVE Center when participation is open, then take on a matched community job site such as raking, trimming, or window washing.
cards.short_summary: Students serve Kirksville residents through matched one-day projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says its SERVE Center matches students with Kirksville job sites for The Big Event, a student-run one-day service project involving tasks such as trimming, raking, and washing windows.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Participation requires registration and assignment through the SERVE Center.

cards.title: The Weathervane That Points Northeast
cards.subtitle: A fixed tribute to Truman’s Northeast Missouri State University history
cards.notes: View Kirk Memorial’s cupola from outside and notice the fixed direction; compare it with the original cupola near the Ruth Towne Museum entrance.
cards.short_summary: A deliberately fixed weathervane preserves a former University name.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman says Kirk Memorial’s weathervane was welded to point northeast when the University was renamed in 1996, and the replacement cupola continued the tradition in 2013.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor campus areas; do not attempt rooftop access.

cards.title: The Midnight Sunken Garden Legend
cards.subtitle: A campus myth attached to benches at Old Baldwin Hall’s former site
cards.notes: Visit the Sunken Garden in daylight, find its benches, and share the lore as a campus story rather than a promise or instruction.
cards.short_summary: A garden at the original Baldwin Hall site carries a marriage-lore myth.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman describes a campus myth that couples who first kiss at midnight on a Sunken Garden bench will eventually marry; the garden marks the first Baldwin Hall site.
cards.source_title: Truman State University Traditions and Lore
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal public campus access hours and respect others using the garden.

cards.title: The Gum Tree’s Exam-Day Lore
cards.subtitle: A Quad tradition with roots in a rule against classroom gum
cards.notes: Find the Gum Tree on the west side of the Quad near the sidewalk and photograph it; treat its good-luck story as lore, not a guarantee.
cards.short_summary: Students historically linked adding gum to a tree with academic luck.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman Today reports that campus lore connected adding gum to the Gum Tree before an exam with good luck or a passing grade; the current tree is on the west side of the Quad.
cards.access_notes: Observe and photograph from the sidewalk; follow current campus guidance and avoid damaging the tree.

cards.title: The Cupola Graduation Photo
cards.subtitle: A former rooftop landmark repurposed as a photo destination
cards.notes: Locate the original cupola outside the Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center and take a respectful photo from the public approach.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors are encouraged to photograph this relocated campus icon.
cards.evidence_claim: Truman Review says the original Kirk Memorial cupola was placed outside the Ruth W. Towne Museum and Visitors Center and that graduating seniors have been encouraged to photograph there in caps and gowns.
cards.access_notes: The cupola is an outdoor photo destination; respect museum operations and other visitors.
